action_items: OPTIONAL (carry-over from iter38): produce-proof runs synchronously in the HTTP thread; a 40-60s ffmpeg render blocks the request. Consider moving to background job + progress-poll for MO-021 v2 (not blocking — current UI shows a spinner and 150s frontend wait completed cleanly).

OPTIONAL (carry-over from iter38): retest_provider() overwrites the status on any transient PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE — tests worked around it with a 5-retry _ensure_pixabay_active(). Recommend only overwriting on CONNECTED/INVALID_KEY/PERMISSION_DENIED.
OPTIONAL: /app/backend/rendered_assets/media_masters accumulates a job dir per produce-proof run — add a retention policy (keep last 5 or those referenced by media_assets).
critical_code_review_comments: scene_matcher._score() applies exclusion filter on TITLE-substring only. If a provider ever returned a candidate with the excluded subject in tags/description but not the title, it could slip through. Current pixabay_video results have subject reflected in title so no live leak observed, but consider extending the check to tags/description strings when available.

media_production.produce_showcase() writes source_doc into db.media_assets BEFORE license_verification check would have blocked (order in code: license check is above download, and download is above insert, so the flow is correct today — however if someone reorders the steps the insert could persist a blocked asset). Consider guarding the insert with an explicit if not blocked.

MediaLibrary.js runProof() sets a UI-side 'Manufacturing… (~40s)' label but has no visible progress-per-stage during the wait — user sees a spinner for the full 40-60s. Consider streaming the produce-proof response (SSE) or polling a job-status endpoint so the founder sees each stage tick in real time (matches the 'transparent' spirit of the panel).

scene_matcher.match() constructs primary_query preferring environmental[0]; both scenes in the forex narration ended up with the SAME query ('global financial district') which returned the same 5 candidates in both scene tiles. Consider dedup / rotation across scenes so a multi-scene product doesn't reuse the same clip for every scene.

MediaLibrary.js registerAsset() still posts collection='QRU General Backgrounds' hardcoded (called from both search results AND scene-matcher approve buttons). Approve-to-Vault from scene matcher should propagate a scene-aware collection (e.g. 'Scene: Risk & Caution').
